'''Lule''' is an indigenous language of northern [[Argentina]], which is now [[extinct language|extinct]]. Campbell (1997) writes that in 1981 there was an unconfirmed report that Lule was still spoken by 5 families in [[Resistencia, Chaco|Resistencia]] in east-central [[Chaco Province]].{{Sfn|Campbell|1997}} It is unclear if it is the same language as ''[[Tonocoté language|Tonocoté]]''.

==Classification==
Lule appears to be distantly related to the still-spoken [[Vilela language]], together forming a small [[Lule–Vilela languages|Lule–Vilela]] family. Kaufman (1990) finds this relationship likely and with general agreement among the major classifiers of South American languages. Viegas Barros published additional evidence 1996–2006. Zamponi (2008) and other authors consider Lule and Vilela two linguistic isolates.

There were three distinct groups known as ''Lulé'':
*The nomadic Lule of the plains, who in addition to their own language, spoke Tonocote, the local lingua franca and the language of Spanish catechism.
*The sedentary Lule of the foothills, who were trilingual in Lule, Tonocote, and Quechua in addition to their original language, [[Cacán language|Cacán]].
*The Lule-Tonocote, whose language was recorded by Machoni.

==Documentation==
In 1586 Father Alonson Bárzana (Bárcena) wrote a grammar of Tonocote, which is now lost. In 1732 Antonio Maccioni (Machoni), who was not aware of Bárzana's grammar, wrote one of his own, ''Arte y vocabulario de la lengua lule y tonocoté'' ('Art and vocabulary of the language of the Lule and Tonocote') of the Lule-Tonocote language at the mission San Esteban de Miraflores.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ARTE Y VOCABULARIO DE LA LENGUA LULE TONOCOTÉ |url=https://pure.mpg.de/rest/items/item_402640_7/component/file_2079520/content |website=pure.mpg.de}}</ref> This is now the primary data on the language. Métraux (1946) concluded that Lule and Tonocote were distinct, and perhaps unrelated, languages, and that the Tonocote at the Miraflores mission had shifted to the Lule language by the time of Machoni.

== Phonology ==
Machoni records a language with vowels {{IPA|/a e i o u/}} and few consonants. Final syllables are stressed. There are consonant clusters in initial and final position: ''quelpç'' {{IPA|[kelpt͡s]}} 'I split', ''slimst'' {{IPA|[slimst]}} 'I blow my nose', ''oalécst'' {{IPA|[waˈlekst]}} 'I know', ''stuç'' {{IPA|[stut͡s]}} 'I throw'. Lule has no postalveolar affricate {{IPA|[t͡ʃ]}}. In the orthography of Machoni, the symbols ''c''',''''' {{Lang|ule|ç}}, and possibly also {{Lang|ule|z}} are used to represent a sound tentatively identified as an alveolar affricate {{IPAblink|t͡s}}. However, {{Lang|ule|c}} is used both for IPA {{IPAblink|t͡s}} and {{IPAblink|k}}, evident from the imperative form of certain verbs, such as {{Lang|ule|uec-y}} {{IPA|[wet͡sˈi]}} 'die!' from {{Lang|ule|uec-ç}} {{IPA|[wet͡st͡s]}} 'I die' versus {{Lang|ule|poqu-y}} {{IPA|[pokˈi]}} 'dig!' from {{Lang|ule|poc-ç}} {{IPA|[pokt͡s]}} 'I dig'. Machoni also adds that in certain words it is pronounced as Spanish {{Lang|es|ç}} or {{Lang|es|ss}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Adelaar |first=Willem F. H. |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/9780511486852/type/book |title=The Languages of the Andes |last2=Muysken |first2=Pieter C. |date=2004-06-10 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-36275-7 |edition=1 |doi=10.1017/cbo9780511486852}}</ref>

The simplicity of the Lule phoneme inventory is unusual compared to that of its relative Vilela, which has postvelar stops, as well as voicing and glottalization distinctions. Machoni may not have recorded such distinctions in his transcriptions. Glottalization in Lule is only suggested by the double consonants in {{Lang|ule|ttá}} 'egg'. Voiceless laterals are evidenced in Machoni's accompanying vocabulary, such as {{Lang|ule|quilhá}} {{IPA|[kiˈɬa]}} 'Indian girl'; cf. Vilela {{Lang|vil|kiɬe}} 'woman' and also possibly a voiceless nasal as seen in {{Lang|ule|nhalá pulú}} 'sugarcane'. Glottal stops are suggested by {{Lang|ule|seç}} ~ {{Lang|ule|s.heç}} {{IPA|[sʔet͡s]}} 'I support', in which {{Lang|ule|s}} and {{Lang|ule|e}} are pronounced separately, and {{Lang|ule|seç}} {{IPA|[set͡s]}} 'I cry', where they are pronounced without separation.<ref name=":0" />
